 Florida's dengue outbreak mirrors a global trend 
 Florida's dengue outbreak mirrors a global trend
 Science Friday | 5 hours ago Play 12 min Download Small Download In Florida, three counties have declared states of emergency due to rising cases of dengue —a viral infection spread by mosquitos carrying the dengue virus. There have been around 1,000 cases in the state this year, making it the largest outbreak in the continental U.S. in decades. 
 But this is part of a larger story. Over the last couple of decades, the number of dengue cases has surged globally, and dengue is becoming more common in places it hasn’t historically been. 
 So what’s behind these shifts? And what public health measures should we be thinking about? Flora chats about this with epidemiologist Gabriela Paz-Bailey, chief of CDC’s dengue branch in San Juan, Puerto Rico. 
 Guest: 
 Dr. Gabriela Paz-Bailey is an epidemiologist and chief of the dengue branch in the Division of Vector-Borne Diseases of the CDC. She’s based in San Juan, Puerto Rico.
